rules.reason: MEMPTR (WZ) is not modelled in 0.2.0. The harness passes the field through, so it diverges wherever the instruction changes WZ.
The Q latch (the flags written by the last instruction) is not modelled; passed through.
The interrupt-acceptance latches (EI delay; LD A,I/R parity bug) are not modelled: Zilion has no interrupts. Passed through.
IM 0/1/2 (and their mirrors) are executed as NOPs; IM is not modelled.

A DD/FD prefix followed by DD, FD or ED is wasted: one step, one M1 cycle, R + 1. Zilion 0.2.0 counts the follower's M1 too and backs PC up, so the follower is counted again next step: R + 2 per wasted prefix. Explained only where the vector says R + 1 and Zilion gives R + 2. SingleStepTests has no such vectors; these come from the analytic set (tools/z80-analytic-vectors.py).
BIT n,(HL) takes F3/F5 from the operand; a Z80 takes them from WZ bits 11 and 13 (MEMPTR leak). Explained only where the vector follows the WZ formula and Zilion the operand formula.
SCF/CCF take F3/F5 from A only; on a Zilog NMOS Z80 they are ((Q xor F) or A) & 0x28, and Q is not modelled. Explained only where the vector follows the NMOS formula and Zilion the A-only formula.

LDIR/LDDR/CPIR/CPDR when repeating: on a Z80, YF = PC.13 and XF = PC.11 (PC = the ED byte); Zilion keeps its non-repeating formula from the data. Explained only where the vector follows the PC rule and Zilion its data formula.
rules.source: design §5.4 and Appendix B (REP-XY); redcode Z80 block flags test

rules.reason: INIR/INDR/OTIR/OTDR when repeating: on a Z80, YF = PC.13 and XF = PC.11 and H and P/V are further adjusted; Zilion keeps its non-repeating formulas. Explained where the vector's X/Y follow the PC rule and Zilion's X/Y its B formula; H and P/V are covered by the mask only (no formula checked).
rules.source: design §5.4 and Appendix B (REP-XY); redcode Z80 block flags test

rules.reason: IN A,(n): port reads return 0 in 0.2.0 (no I/O device). Explained only where the vector's port supplies a non-zero value, the vector's A holds it and Zilion's A is 0. Tests whose port reads 0 must match.

IN r,(C) and IN (C): the port reads 0 in 0.2.0. Explained only where the port value is non-zero, the vector's target register holds it, Zilion's holds 0 with the flags of a 0 read (Z, P/V; C kept), and every other register matches.

INI/IND/INIR/INDR: the port reads 0 in 0.2.0, so the byte stored at (HL) and the flags derived from it differ. Explained only where the port value is non-zero, the vector stores it at (HL), Zilion stores 0 with its flag formula for a 0 read, and no other address differs.
The 0.2.0 core never calls a port-read hook, so the vector's listed port read does not happen.
The 0.2.0 core never calls a port-write hook, so the vector's port write does not happen.
